Title: HtmlSanitizer URL Host Validation Bypass via Backslash / Redundant Slash Obfuscation
Analysis: The `UrlSanitizer::sanitize` function in `Symfony\Component\HtmlSanitizer\TextSanitizer\UrlSanitizer` allows attackers to bypass the `$allowedHosts` restriction when `$allowRelative` is enabled (which is a common configuration to allow relative links like `/about`). ### Data Flow & Reachability Analysis 1. **Source**: An untrusted user inputs HTML containing a link or media element with a maliciously crafted URL, such as: - `https:\\\\evil.com` - `https://///evil.com` These reach the `HtmlSanitizer::sanitize()` or `HtmlSanitizer::sanitizeFor()` entry points. 2. **Parser Deviation (The Flaw)**: - The sanitizer uses `League\Uri\UriString::parse()` to extract the components of the URL. - For `https:\\\\evil.com`, the backslashes confuse the parser. Since the parser doesn't normalize backslashes for the host, it parses the URL as: `['scheme' => 'https', 'host' => null, 'path' => '\\\\evil.com']` - For `https://///evil.com`, the redundant slashes lead to an empty host name: `['scheme' => 'https', 'host' => '']` 3. **Skipped Validation (The Bypass)**: - In `UrlSanitizer::sanitize()`: - The check `if (!$allowRelative && !$url['scheme'])` is bypassed because `$url['scheme']` is `'https'`. - The check `if (!$allowRelative && !$url['host'])` is bypassed because `$allowRelative` is `true`. - The check `if ($url['host'] && null !== $allowedHosts && !self::isAllowedHost(...))` is bypassed because `$url['host']` is either `null` or `''` (both of which are falsy). - As a result, the domain name `evil.com` is never checked against the list of `$allowedHosts`. 4. **Sink**: - `UrlSanitizer::sanitize()` returns the original/reconstructed string `https:\\\\evil.com` or `https://///evil.com` untouched. - This URL is emitted in the sanitized HTML output (e.g. ``). 5. **Browser Normalization (Exploitation)**: - Modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) strictly implement the WHATWG URL specification. Under this specification, backslashes after a special scheme (like `http` or `https`) are normalized to forward slashes, and redundant forward slashes are collapsed. - Thus, a browser rendering `` or `` will normalize the destination to `https://evil.com/` and navigate the user to the attacker-controlled server upon click, bypassing the allowed hosts restriction (leading to Open Redirect or loading arbitrary external resources if used on images/media). ### Conceptual Exploit Payload Assuming `allowedHosts` is configured to `['trusted.com']` and `allowRelative` is enabled: ```html Click here to continue Click here to continue ```
